title: A higher box energy level
hook: Change quantum number and predict energy eigenvalue.
misconception: energy eigenvalue doubles when quantum number doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply E_n = n²h²/(8mL²) to compare energy eigenvalue when quantum number changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a particle in a one-dimensional infinite square well of fixed width and mass with allowed positive integer quantum numbers, E_n = n²h²/(8mL²). When quantum number doubles, energy eigenvalue becomes 4 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model E_n = n²h²/(8mL²); scaling exponent 2. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a particle in a one-dimensional infinite square well of fixed width and mass with allowed positive integer quantum numbers, with a nonzero initial result. If quantum number triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on energy eigenvalue?
recall.why: Apply E_n = n²h²/(8mL²) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 9.
